messages:
incident-bot: :warning: ALERT: Multiple CUDA illegal memory access events observed on serving-node-47 (gpu0) starting 23:12 UTC. Auto-evacuation policy triggered for pods with model=v2.
Aisha (oncall): saw the alert. spikes in OOM/killed containers too?
Miguel: yes, several containers restarted, kubelet showing oom_kill and then GPU illegal-access oom traces.
Jen K: logs look like kernel reports immediately before container crash. attaching small dmesg snippet.
Jen K: ```
[ 3178.123456] GPU0: illegal memory access at 0x7fabc000 (pc 0x7f1a2b3c)
[ 3178.123458] RIP: 0x7f1a2b3c in gpu_kernel_fn+0x2c
[ 3178.123460] BUG: kernel NULL pointer deref in smmu pagewalk?
```
Ravi: possible pagewalk / SMMU race, but also seeing prefix-cache pressure in runtime. sequence lengths jumped, KV cache thrash.
Ops Lead: customer impact? any 5xx spikes?
Maya (CS): one customer reported degraded responses ~23:10-23:25 UTC (api timeouts). tentative list: accounts A-23, B-99.
Aisha (oncall): immediate plan: 1) cordon node 47, 2) drain pods to alternate nodes, 3) pin affected customers to fallback model (v2-quant) for safety, 4) disable prefix/KV cache for v2 on remaining nodes. I'll take point.
Miguel: +1. cordoning now. command: `kubectl cordon serving-node-47`
Aisha (oncall): running drain (graceful) `kubectl drain serving-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
incident-bot: NOTE: drain triggered by oncall at 23:15:18 UTC. Evacuation started.
Jen K: while draining, observed another illegal access logged by container runtime before it terminated. attaching container log snippet: ```ERROR Runtime: cudaIllegalAccess at out_of_bounds_kv(); backtrace ...```
Ravi: hypothesis: a kernel-level misalignment in driver + accelerated kernel path that surfaces under heavy KV cache reuse and long prefix seq. reproduces with stress pattern?
Miguel: can we repro on staging with same seq distribution? spinning up a stress job now.
Ops Lead: mitigation hold windows: don't rollout v2 until we validate a fix or implement safe fallback. Toggle rollout gates.
Aisha (oncall): implementing immediate traffic steering: update route policy to send traffic for model=v2 -> v2-quant fallback. `redwoodctl route update --model v2 --fallback v2-quant --sticky-customer A-23,B-99`
deploy-bot: Route update job started (job-id: rdu-8793).
Maya (CS): telling impacted customers we've routed them to a fallback model; wants ETA before we switch them back.
Aisha (oncall): ETA: 1hr for full triage; we'll keep them on fallback until we confirm no illegal-access on nodes.
Miguel: stress job on staging hitting similar sequences reproduced a kernel oops but at lower frequency. collecting kernel traces and perf counters.
Jen K: grabbed pstack + nvcrash logs, putting them in #eng-runtime/sandbox. suspicion: a race in kernel pagewalk when SMMU entries are being torn down during preemption.
Ravi: workaround to reduce exposure: 1) disable KV cache, 2) reduce batch_size to 1 for v2 on all nodes, 3) disable continuous batching for v2. That should reduce aggressive memory access patterns.
Aisha (oncall): applying config changes to live: `redwoodctl model-config set v2 --kv-cache=false --batch-size=1 --continuous-batching=false --apply`
incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: model v2 kv-cache=false batch-size=1 applied at 23:22:41 UTC by Aisha.
Miguel: confirming reduces error rate on staging run. errors dropped from ~8/hr to ~1/hr. not perfect but much better.
Ops Lead: will coordinate kernel team and upstream vendor. raise bug with driver/kernel with attached logs.
Jen K: opening internal bug now and CC'ing kernel vendor. issue-1234 created: "SMMU/pagewalk race causing illegal device addr under KV-cache pressure".
Aisha (oncall): handoff to Miguel for triage and long-term mitigation. I'm wrapping up immediate evac and putting ticket in followup.
Aisha (oncall): Miguel, you're owner for next 8 hours. please update incident channel with status.
Miguel: taking it. immediate next steps: full trace capture (ftrace + perf), coordinate with kernel vendor, test a kernel patch and validate on staging, then plan safe rollout.
Maya (CS): thanks, will update customers: fallback model in place, reduced risk, next update in 1 hour.
incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: customer-impact window 23:10-23:25 UTC. impacted customers: [A-23,B-99], approx 12 requests failed, autoscaled fallbacks served ~120 requests.
Ops Lead: postmortem owners: Miguel (triage), Jen K (logs/traces), Ravi (runtime config), Aisha (incident coord), Maya (customer comms). Target postmortem draft in 72 hours.
Miguel: creating canary plan: after kernel/vendor patch, verify on 3 nodes, run 6h soak, then incrementally re-enable kv-cache & batching.
Aisha (oncall): closing immediate on-call handoff. will remain reachable. thanks all. :thumbsup:
Jen K: small follow-up: keep an eye on pod OOM score settings and gpu pci recovery logs; those looked noisy.
Ravi: noted. also suggest temporary extra margin on eviction thresholds to reduce thrash during drain.
Miguel: logging next update here by 02:30 UTC with vendor response or staging results.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (live mitigations applied): node cordoned, pods drained, v2 routed to v2-quant fallback, runtime configs adjusted.
